note: Acervo ships this list of providers, never a credential. `keyEnv` and `requires` name environment variables; a value never appears here, and neither does an account, project or billing id — this repository is public, so a console link is a template filled in from the environment. Order is the fallback order, and the unit is a (provider, model) pair rather than a provider: with ACERVO_TEXT_CHAIN unset the walk is provider by provider and, inside each, model by model, because a free tier is metered per model — two models with 500 requests a day each are a thousand requests a day, and the second is reached by the first one's 429.

providers.label: Gemini (free tier)
providers.notes: Two text models at 500 requests a day each, which is why both are listed rather than one: they are separate buckets, so the second is a genuine thousand-a-day rather than a spare. Speech is one model at 10 a day — enough for a handful of words, not for a batch. The tier allows a second speech model, `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts`, and it is deliberately not listed: it answers a short word with generated *text* often enough to be useless, which Gemini then refuses with a 400, and LiteLLM's speech bridge surfaces that as an IndexError rather than as a refusal — so the chain would read it as terminal and stop rather than falling through. Prompting it as a transcript instruction does not help. Worth revisiting in plan 06, which is where audio gets a caller. There is deliberately no `image` kind: on this tier every image model, Nano Banana included, is allowed 0 requests, so listing one would put a row in the chain that can only 429. Voice names do not carry across providers, so the row names one Gemini accepts; a caller that asks for a specific voice overrides it. Temperature is deliberately unset: LiteLLM recommends leaving Gemini 3+ at its default.

providers.label: Vertex AI
providers.notes: Application default credentials, not an API key: LiteLLM has no Vertex express-key path (BerriAI/litellm#21036). Present on a workstation that has run `gcloud auth application-default login`; on a server it needs a service-account JSON and GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. This is the only row that can generate an image today, the free tier having no image allowance at all. The image model is a Gemini one rather than Imagen, no Imagen id being reachable in this project, and it is also what the sense-image pipeline already uses. Location stays `global`; the Gemini image models 404 in a named region. The text models are the ones this project actually has: `gemini-3-flash` and `gemini-3.1-flash` both 404 here, and `gemini-3.8-flash` is what the sense-image pipeline already asks for briefs. Being paid rather than metered, the second model is availability cover rather than a second quota. There is no `reasoning_effort`: the REST call this replaced sent `thinkingLevel: MEDIUM`, but LiteLLM refuses the parameter for `gemini-3-flash` outright, and `params` is where it goes back if that changes.

providers.label: Cloudflare Workers AI
providers.notes: Workers AI has no account-less endpoint, so the account id is required as well as the token — and it is what makes the usage link point at the right dashboard. LiteLLM covers text only: image and audio go through the hand-written adapter, because FLUX.2 Klein needs multipart/form-data even for a text-only prompt. Audio is Deepgram Aura rather than melotts: melotts answers Spanish with AiError 8002 and answered a plain English word with a 500. Aura takes `text` where melotts took `prompt`. The model ids here are the ones that answered a live call; the rest of Workers AI's catalogue is unverified.

providers.label: OpenAI
providers.notes: Listed, not verified: no live call has been made against this row.

providers.label: OpenRouter
providers.notes: One key in front of many models. Whether a schema is honoured depends on the model behind it, so this row claims the weaker guarantee. Listed, not verified.

providers.label: Ollama (this machine)
providers.notes: No credential, but declared rather than assumed: the row is available only where ACERVO_OLLAMA_URL says a server is listening. A row that were always available would make `capture_unavailable` unreachable and would send every exhausted chain at a port that is usually closed. There is no usage link because there is no bill. Plan 07 is where a local model runs somewhere other than this machine.
